sections.title: Date and Time of Discharge
sections.promptHint: Doctor enters manually when starting the draft; DisDate in the system is empty until the hospital finalizes discharge.

sections.title: Diagnosis
sections.promptHint: List the primary dermatological diagnosis first, then secondaries. Use exact clinical wording; do not add or reclassify diagnoses.

sections.title: Presenting Complaints
sections.promptHint: Summarize distinct complaints of type 'Chief Complaint' only. Collapse repeated rows with the same complaint into one clean line, adding the recorded date or date range when useful. Preserve the recorded skin-related wording; do not include associated complaints or dump raw rows. Return one item per line; do not leave an escaped-newline marker visible in the text.

sections.title: History of Present Illness
sections.promptHint: Write a concise chronological History of Present Illness using the chief complaints plus associated complaints and recorded remarks, emphasizing the documented evolution of skin findings, onset, distribution, itching, and treatments tried. Group repeated symptoms rather than listing every row. Return 2-4 useful lines separated by real line breaks. Use only this recorded proxy, do not invent detail, and do not replace the narrative with a disclaimer. Add at most one short review caveat at the end if needed.

sections.title: Past Medical History
sections.promptHint: Summarize the distinct recorded problems as a concise Past Medical History, including status and onset and noting prior dermatological conditions such as eczema when present. Use one problem per line, do not invent or reclassify conditions, and add at most one short review caveat at the end if needed.

sections.title: Current Medication
sections.promptHint: List active medications using medication name, recorded schedule, start date, stop date, and route when recorded. Group repeated orders for the same medication and route into one compact line, combining distinct schedules or dates when needed. Reconcile active orders with explicit note-recorded medications; note-only facts are provisional and require doctor verification in the source panel. Include topical treatments when recorded, omit status, and do not invent dose or route.

sections.title: Personal History
sections.promptHint: No source in the API. Leave blank for the doctor; never invent habits or lifestyle detail.

sections.title: Family History
sections.promptHint: No source in the API. Leave blank for the doctor; never invent family history of atopy or psoriasis.

sections.title: Allergies
sections.promptHint: List each allergen with reaction nature and symptoms — drug allergies matter for future dermatological prescribing — or state the recorded status (e.g. NKA).

sections.title: Occupational History
sections.promptHint: No source in the API. Leave blank for the doctor; never invent occupational or irritant-exposure detail.

sections.title: On Examination
sections.promptHint: Most recent vitals only, and state explicitly this covers recorded vitals, not a skin examination. Where skin findings are mentioned they must come only from recorded complaints and notes; do not invent morphology, distribution, or erythema descriptors.

sections.title: Course in Hospital
sections.promptHint: Synthesize notes, labs, radiology, medication changes, and the vitals trend into 3-6 concise chronological lines separated by real line breaks. Emphasize recorded skin-directed therapy, fever, and infection markers that drove changes. Do not reproduce raw lists or a medication list here; stick strictly to the data.

sections.title: Condition at Discharge
sections.promptHint: Most recent vitals plus current status of active problems. Report recorded values; do not overstate skin improvement without recorded evidence.

sections.title: Medications During Stay
sections.promptHint: List medication facts recorded during this episode, including explicit medications in clinical notes when no order exists. Group repeated orders for the same medication and route into one compact line, combining distinct schedules, dates, or statuses when needed. Note-only facts require doctor verification in the source panel; do not include raw JSON.

sections.title: Medications on Discharge
sections.promptHint: Draft a concise medication-on-discharge list using active discharge-suitable orders plus explicit active oral/topical medications recorded in notes. Group repeated orders for the same medication and route into one compact line. Exclude injections, IV/infusion/chemotherapy, inpatient-only supplies, and any medication not present in the reconciled facts. Note-only medications require doctor verification in the source panel. Use medication name, schedule, start date, and stop date; omit status and do not invent replacements.

sections.title: Advice
sections.promptHint: Draft short patient-specific advice from explicit advice, restrictions, precautions, or instructions in progress/discharge notes, using dermatological diagnoses only as context. If notes lack explicit advice, provide only a concise diagnosis-grounded draft for doctor review; do not invent doses or restrictions.

sections.title: Special Needs
sections.promptHint: No source in the API. Leave blank for the doctor; never invent care needs.

sections.title: Follow Up Advice
sections.promptHint: Draft dermatology follow-up advice only when the notes contain an explicit follow-up instruction. Use the recorded wording and do not invent a clinic, interval, test, or treatment change. If no explicit follow-up instruction is recorded, return an empty string.
